clue.text: At turn of century, papacy was best place to start

definitions.meaning: around 2000 the Pope, John Paul II, was Polish, so the papacy was the post held by a Pole
in motor racing the front spot on the starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier

explanation.surface: A remark on the papacy around the year 2000 being a prime spot from which to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as a Pole's position: John Paul II, Pope from 1978 to 2005, was from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Formula One the pole is the first grid slot, the most favoured starting spot in a race.

clue.text: Eat this hat? A fib, some say

definitions.meaning: a savoury pastry filled with minced meat, made to be eaten
a round felt hat with a flat crown and a turned-up brim
'porky pie' is rhyming slang for a lie, so some people say this for a fib

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether to eat a hat, followed by a claim that this is a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions. A PORK PIE is a British cold meat pastry; the PORK PIE hat is a style; 'porky (pie)' is Cockney rhyming slang for 'lie', hence 'some say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastry, the felt hat style and the rhyming-slang word for a lie all share this name.

clue.text: Organ is musical, none the less

indicators.note: less means the following item is taken away from the show title

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart stage musical based on Oliver Twist
none is nil, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A claim that an organ is no less musical for all that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like the phrase 'nonetheless'; split it so 'none' is O and 'less' removes it, with 'the' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large internal organ of the body that filters the blood.

clue.text: Undress to get into long business suit

indicators.note: to get into means the undressing word goes inside the yearning word

parts.note: to long for is to pine
to undress is to strip

explanation.surface: Advice to take off your clothes and climb into a long business suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe is a suit cloth with fine vertical lines, the classic outfit of the City banker.

clue.text: Proposed arrangement, finding machines not in working order

indicators.note: the remaining letters are set working into a new order
not in says the letters of the word in are dropped from the machines

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a plan discovers the machines are broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in working order' reads as 'broken', but 'not in' takes I and N out of MACHINES, and the MACHES left are put in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline plan or diagrammatic representation of how things are to be organised.

clue.text: Time that's coming to cut grass —- get men right in

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the soldiers and the right inside the grass-cutting word

parts.note: to cut grass is to mow
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A reminder that the grass needs cutting soon, so round up some men for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is only a link; the men and right letters go inside the mowing word after its first letter, and 'in' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow is the day after today, time that is still to come.

clue.text: Cereal tucked into by English man who achieved I ac

indicators.note: tucked into by means the cereal is entered by the letter for English

parts.note: oats are a cereal crop

explanation.surface: An Englishman with a hearty appetite digs into his breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to 1 across: Captain Lawrence Oates of Scott's Antarctic expedition reached the South Pole, a Pole position.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Oates, of Scott's 1912 expedition, reached the South Pole before dying on the return journey.

clue.text: Clergyman swallowed one -—- very health-giving

indicators.note: swallowed means the churchman takes the other letters inside him

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish clergyman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A clergyman swallowed something, and it did him a great deal of good.
explanation.definitionFit: Curative means healing, tending to cure illness and so restore health.

clue.text: A few coins in place of business

definitions.meaning: small coins carried in the pocket, loose cash
an exchange where merchants trade, often shortened with an apostrophe

explanation.surface: Some loose coins found at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change, short for Exchange, is an old name for a trading hall such as the Royal Exchange in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coinage is loose cash, and the trading hall sense is an old clipped form of exchange.

clue.text: Flier lacking courage leaving the front

indicators.note: leaving the front means the first letter departs from the cowardly word

parts.note: craven means cowardly, lacking courage

explanation.surface: A pilot loses his nerve and abandons the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird, and any bird is a flier in crossword terms.

clue.text: In reality, unwelcome news

parts.note: at home means in, as in staying in
reality is the truth

explanation.surface: A remark that, in reality, the news is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unpleasant fact about oneself that one would rather not hear.

clue.text: Break watch that only works occasionally

parts.note: to break is to part, separate
a watch is a timer

explanation.surface: A broken watch that only runs some of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-timer is a worker employed for only some of the hours of a full working week.

clue.text: Offence, staying with a lover

indicators.note: staying means holding, so the offence keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: an offence against God is a sin

explanation.surface: Someone commits an offence by staying with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a young male lover or suitor, a poetic word for a country youth courting.

clue.text: Priest's laboured wit

indicators.note: laboured suggests the letters have been worked over into a new shape

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A clergyman's jokes are heavy and forced.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is liveliness of mind and quickness of wit, borrowed from French.

clue.text: No Iolanthe performance could be so superb

definitions.text: No Iolanthe performance could be so
definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe has a chorus of members of the House of Lords, so a show without them would lack its lords

explanation.surface: A critic's praise for a staging of the operetta Iolanthe.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta whose chorus are peers of the realm; with no peers it would be peer-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, so excellent that nothing matches it.

clue.text: Fail to come up to establish an official record

parts.note: to fail to do something is not to do it
to come up is to arise

explanation.surface: A note about something that never cropped up on the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To notarise a document is to have a notary certify it, making it an official attested record.

clue.text: Permitted nothing to be settled immediately

definitions.meaning: read as two words, it says every debt may be owed rather than paid at once

explanation.surface: A note that one may defer paying any bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ALL OWABLE: everything can be owed, so nothing need be settled immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allowable is permissible, within the rules.

clue.text: Crashing bore — I ran off the ground

indicators.note: crashing suggests these letters are smashed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tedious person causes a crash, and someone flees the scene of the accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne means carried by the air, in flight and no longer on the ground.

clue.text: Malignant woman to abandon her wicked ways

parts.note: to shed something is to cast it off or abandon it
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: A wicked woman is urged to give up her bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is a link joining the pieces; the surface pictures reform, the wordplay simply sets SHED beside EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a cruel, spiteful woman, a female fiend.

clue.text: Fight with energy in tricky situation

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A vigorous brawl in an awkward predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament one has got into, a fix or jam.

clue.text: Priestly vestment's fastening back to front, though

parts.note: an alb is a white linen vestment worn by priests

indicators.note: back to front means the fastening word is turned around

parts.note: a tie is a fastening

explanation.surface: A priest's robe has its fastening at the back rather than the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning although or even though.

clue.text: Helper supports child without reserve

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supports another by lying beneath it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an ally is a helper

explanation.surface: An assistant looks after a youngster with complete devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely, wholly and with nothing held back.

clue.text: In Shakespeare, conspirator dropping us for old lieutenant

indicators.note: dropping, with for, says one pair of letters gives way to another

parts.note: Cassius is a conspirator against Caesar in Julius Caesar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark on a Shakespeare plotter being swapped out for a former officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping us for old' replaces US in CASSIUS with O. Cassio is Othello's lieutenant, so 'In Shakespeare' places both characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassio is the lieutenant whom Iago schemes against in Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: One may venerate this prophet, believer held

indicators.note: held means the believer holds the prophet within it

parts.note: RC, a Roman Catholic, is a believer
Eli is the Old Testament priest and prophet who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: A believer clings to a prophet whom he reveres.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a saint's remains or belongings, kept and venerated by the faithful.

clue.text: Coconut crop developed before mid-May

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked into a new form
mid picks out the centre letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A coconut harvest maturing before the middle of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply puts CORP (from crop, 'developed') ahead of A, the middle of MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, pressed for coconut oil.

clue.text: Sausage split to see temperature in uncooked inside

indicators.note: inside puts the raw-with-temperature piece within the split word

parts.note: to burst is to split open

indicators.note: in places the temperature letter inside the uncooked word

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: Checking the temperature of a split sausage to see if it is raw in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link. 'in' and 'inside' are two container signals, one nested within the other, giving RATW inside the split word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bratwurst is a German sausage of pork or veal, usually grilled.

clue.text: Soulless worker is British in origin

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for British within the origin word

parts.note: the root of something is its origin

explanation.surface: A heartless employee is said to be British by birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine that does work but has no soul or feelings.

clue.text: Having admission documents, succeed in taking in game

indicators.note: taking in means the succeed word encloses the game word

parts.note: to pass a test is to succeed
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Someone holding entry papers succeeds in getting into a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Passports are official documents that allow their holders to be admitted to foreign countries.

clue.text: Unfinished tower left by child

indicators.note: by means the left letter is placed beside the child

parts.note: a babe is a baby or small child

explanation.surface: A child abandons a half-built tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of Babel in Genesis was never completed, as God confused the builders' languages.

clue.text: Chap using force I left with ill-will

parts.note: a chap is a male

indicators.note: left means the letter for I has departed from the forceful word

parts.note: doing something using force is doing it violently

explanation.surface: A man resorts to force and departs in a spiteful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolently means in a spiteful manner, wishing harm to others.
